title: Blocking std::fs I/O inside async fn without spawn_blocking
description:
Synchronous filesystem calls run directly on the tokio runtime inside `async fn` bodies, stalling the reactor thread for the duration of the syscall.

persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs — `scan_token_caches()` (line 96) is a plain sync fn doing `std::fs::read_to_string` on up to three files (lines 106, 119) plus JSON parsing of each. It is called from three async trait methods: `enumerate()` (line 163), `prove()` (line 173), and `freshness()` (line 190). An Azure MSAL cache is routinely a few hundred KiB and lives on whatever the user's $HOME is mounted on — an NFS or autofs home hangs the whole runtime, not just this task. `prove()` and `freshness()` re-scan from disk on every call, so this is on the hot path.

persona-grpc/src/server.rs:18-32 — `async fn serve` calls `std::fs::remove_file`, `std::fs::create_dir_all`, and `std::fs::set_permissions`. One-shot at startup, so low impact, but `tokio::fs` is a drop-in here.

The rest of the crate already does this correctly: fido2.rs:64 wraps the blocking device enumeration in `spawn_blocking`, and gpg.rs:105 uses `tokio::process::Command`. oidc.rs is the outlier.

Fix: wrap `scan_token_caches()` in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` at its three call sites (or make it async over `tokio::fs`), and switch server.rs to `tokio::fs`. Cheap `Path::exists()` probes (ssh.rs:35, tailscale.rs:29) are a single stat and can stay.
close_reason:
Fixed in b251a07 for the hot path; server.rs deliberately left alone.

DONE: scan_token_caches now runs via tokio::task::spawn_blocking at both call sites. A JoinError (the scan panicked) is reported as AttestorError::Unavailable rather than propagating into the caller's task.

BEAD IS STALE on the call sites: it says three async methods call it -- enumerate() at line 163, prove() at 173, freshness() at 190. There are TWO: enumerate at 152 and freshness at 157. OidcCachedAttestor does not implement prove() at all; it inherits the trait's default (persona-attestors/src/lib.rs:112), which returns ChallengeFailed without touching the filesystem.

NOT DONE, deliberately: converting persona-grpc/src/server.rs to tokio::fs. The bead concedes it is one-shot at startup. It is more than that -- those calls now live in bind_listener (added in 56efa94), which runs while binding, before the server accepts anything, so there is no other task to stall. tokio::fs is spawn_blocking underneath, so the conversion would buy nothing and add async plumbing to a synchronous function. Recorded in the commit message so it is not re-proposed.

NO TEST for the actual property. Demonstrating that the scan no longer occupies a reactor thread needs it to be slow enough for a sibling task to observe progress during it, which is a timing race; a flaky test is worse than an absent one, and the property is spawn_blocking's documented contract. What IS tested is the plumbing -- that the scan round-trips through the blocking pool and returns -- and it is mutation-verified two ways (helper always errors; scan panics inside the pool). oidc.rs had no tests at all before this.
